format.note: Triple round-robin: 10 clubs meet three times (27 matches). Extra home games are drawn before the season. Calendar-year, March-October.
Triple round-robin, 27 matches. Field is dominated by reserve sides (B36 II, HB II, KI II, Vikingur II, NSI II, etc.).

boundaries.note: Two direct places each way: bottom two of the Premier League are relegated, top two of 1. deild promoted. No play-off (one existed from 1995 to 2005). Only non-reserve clubs can be promoted; if a relegated club already has a reserve side in 1. deild, that reserve side drops a division instead, which reprieves another club.

conflicts.detail: 1. deild is mostly reserve sides. A reserve team cannot be promoted, and there is only relegation from the top flight if at least one non-reserve club finishes in the 1. deild top three. If the top two are both reserve sides, the third-placed eligible club comes up instead.

If a club is relegated from the Premier League and already has a reserve team in 1. deild, the reserve team is moved down a division to make room. That can save another club from relegation, so the nominal 2 down / 2 up is not always 2/2 in practice.

Both levels are 10 clubs playing each other three times (27 matches), with the extra home games drawn before the season rather than decided by the previous table. A double round-robin model (18) understates the season by a third.

notes: Calendar-year 2026 season, complete at the research date. Sizes 10/10 and levels match our rows. 1. deild relegates two to the 2. deild (level 3, not modelled). Cups and UEFA competitions excluded.
